chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Do not eat the slaughtered meat of the Arab Christians, for they are not People of the Book.
ai.seo_question: Why are Arab Christians not considered People of the Book for the purpose of eating their slaughtered meat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this chain linking Imam al-Baqir to Ali ibn Abi Talib, establishing a specific juristic distinction where 'Arab Christians' are excluded from the general permissibility of *Ahl al-Kitab* meat. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that tribal identity and specific historical contexts can affect the status of religious communities, distinguishing them from the broader category of People of the Book mentioned in the Quran.
